chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Initiating the greeting (al-salam) is voluntary, and responding to it is an obligation.'

key_terms.السَّلَامُ: The Islamic greeting 'al-salam alaykum' (peace be upon you); here referring to the act of initiating the salutation
key_terms.تَطَوُّع: Voluntary/supererogatory act (tatawwu'); recommended but not obligatory
key_terms.فَرِيضَة: An obligatory duty (farida); a binding religious obligation

ai.seo_question: Is it obligatory to respond to the Islamic greeting (salam) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits a prophetic hadith that establishes the jurisprudential ruling on the Islamic greeting: initiating the salam is a recommended voluntary act (sunnah), while responding to a greeting is a wajib (obligatory) duty. This hadith served as a foundational legal text for scholars determining the different levels of Islamic obligation regarding greetings. The Quran (4:86) had already commanded that when greeted, one must respond with an equal or better greeting, and this hadith specifies that responding is thus binding.
